key_insight: A small set of retrieved, category-relevant examples used to augment vision–language prompts can substantially close the performance gap between zero-shot open-vocabulary segmentation and fully supervised approaches.
problem_solved: Overcomes the limitations of coarse image-level supervision and semantic ambiguity in text prompts that prevent VLMs from delivering accurate pixel-level (open-vocabulary) segmentation.
method: Define a few-shot setting that augments textual prompts with a small number of retrieved exemplars (image ± mask) relevant to the target category.
Retrieve category-relevant examples from an external pool and fuse exemplar information with VLM features to guide pixel-level prediction.
Calibrate or adapt segmentation outputs using the few-shot cues to resolve linguistic ambiguity and refine masks without full supervision.
impact: Enables substantially better open-vocabulary segmentation with only a handful of labeled examples, reducing annotation costs and improving adaptability to novel categories for practitioners and deployed systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: query text → retrieval of 3–5 exemplar (image+mask) pairs → fusion with VLM → pixel-wise segmentation output
Before/after qualitative examples: ambiguous text prompt showing coarse zero-shot mask vs. refined few-shot mask
Performance chart: accuracy/IoU bars comparing zero-shot, few-shot (this method), and fully supervised baselines
Retrieval illustration: gallery of exemplar thumbnails with highlighted matches to the query category
paper_title: Retrieve and Segment: Are a Few Examples Enough to Bridge the Supervision Gap in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation?
paper_authors: Tilemachos Aravanis, Vladan Stojnić, Bill Psomas, Nikos Komodakis, Giorgos Tolias
